key_insight: First-principles calculations predict that full hydrogenation converts metallic irida-graphene into irida-graphane, an indirect wide-band-gap semiconductor with a 6.0 eV HSE06 gap.
engineering_relevance: Predicted visible transparency and strong deep-ultraviolet absorption make irida-graphane a candidate for UV optoelectronics and transparent coatings.
method: PBE and HSE06 density functional theory calculations
Phonon analysis and ab initio molecular dynamics
Structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical characterization
evidence_signal: Calculations show no imaginary phonon frequencies, structural integrity in AIMD up to 2000 K, visible reflectivity below 0.3%, and deep-UV absorption coefficients of 10⁵–10⁶ cm⁻¹.
watch_item: The predictions require experimental validation, particularly synthesis with complete hydrogenation and the proposed hydrogen arrangement.
paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
